title: Logical Reasoning
seo_title: Logical Reasoning – SSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Recognise simple and compound statements; find negations; write the converse, inverse and contrapositive; find truth values; draw valid conclusions. (summary of the NERDC SSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 1 maths worksheets on logical reasoning: negation, converse, inverse and contrapositive, truth values with and, or and implies, and valid conclusions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: p ⇒ q is false only when p is true and q is false
key_sub: The contrapositive ~q ⇒ ~p means the same as p ⇒ q.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A statement is either true or false. Its negation has the opposite truth value.
  • For “if p, then q”: the converse is “if q, then p”; the contrapositive is “if not q, then not p”.
  • p ∧ q (and) is true only when both are true; p ∨ q (or) is true when at least one is true.

Examples

Example

Negation of “All boys like football.”

Not all boys do

Answer: Some boys do not like football.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking the converse is always trueOnly the contrapositive always has the same truth value.
Negating “all” as “none”The negation of “all” is “some … not”.
Thinking p ⇒ q is false when p is falseIt is true whenever p is false.

faq.q: Is the contrapositive equivalent to the statement?

faq.a: One whose conclusion must be true when the premises are true.

items.q: Statement: “If Ngozi practises every day, then she will win the race.” Which is its inverse?
c: If Ngozi does not practise every day, then she will not win the race.
If she will win the race, then Ngozi practises every day.
If she will not win the race, then Ngozi does not practise every day.
If Ngozi practises every day, then she will win the race.
items.e: The inverse makes both parts negative without swapping them: If Ngozi does not practise every day, then she will not win the race.

items.q: Premises: All prime numbers greater than 2 are odd. 13 is a prime number greater than 2. What is a valid conclusion?
items.e: The conclusion must follow from the premises: 13 is odd.

items.e: The converse swaps the two parts: If the shop is closed, then it is Sunday.

items.q: Statement: “If Chidi is late, then he will miss the bus.” Which is its inverse?
c: If Chidi is late, then he will miss the bus.

items.e: The inverse makes both parts negative without swapping them: If Chidi is not late, then he will not miss the bus.
